title: One-line runbook + sprint docket
content:
Purpose: super compact personal ledger for a focused sprint — capture runs, quick signals, and immediate next steps. Keep this as the single source for quick copy-paste into PR descriptions or Slack updates.

Format notes: each run is a 1-line capsule: runID | model | q (quant) | batch | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | cost/1k tok | success% | short note / follow-up. Use shorthand.

-- Runs (chronological, newest at top) --
R-20251107-09 | redwood-v1-7b | int4 | 16 | 48 | 120 | $0.32 | 98% | good perf on long prefix, small bump when cache miss
R-20251107-06 | redwood-v1-13b | q4_0 | 8 | 95 | 230 | $0.88 | 93% | quality OK; cost high, try int4 + small-batch autotune
R-20251106-18 | redwood-v1-7b | int8 | 32 | 60 | 150 | $0.42 | 97% | stable latency, worse cost than int4
R-20251105-11 | llama-2-7b | q4_1 | 12 | 70 | 160 | $0.39 | 92% | hallucination cases on bullet lists, flag set A
R-20251103-02 | redwood-v1-7b | int4 | 4 | 35 | 90 | $0.28 | 99% | excellent for short prompts; try async-batching 8
R-20251029-14 | redwood-v1-7b | int4 | 64 | 110 | 290 | $0.25 | 94% | throughput good but tail latency spikes - investigate batching window
R-20251025-01 | redwood-trim-3b | fp16 | 64 | 140 | 400 | $0.12 | 88% | cheap but quality regression on instruction-following

Quick takeaways (one-line):
- int4 + small batch (4-16) gives best latency:cost sweet spot for short-interactive flows.
- Larger batches (>=32) reduce token cost but introduce p95 tail — tune batching window and async flush.
- 13b gives better quality but >2.5x cost for modest quality gains; consider distillation/trim for mid-range.
- KV-cache hit rate is the single biggest perf lever for our dialogue workloads — capture hit% next run.

Immediate todo (this sprint):
- Add column for KV-cache-hit% and rerun R-20251107-09 with cache instrumentation (owner: me)
- Try autoscale batch schedule: warm-up-batches=8, flush-ms=18 (experiment param set: AUTOBATCH-18)
- Create short eval set (15 prompts) for hallucination quick-check and attach to PR 784

Quick formulas / macros (handy):
- cost_per_1k = (instance_cost_per_token * 1000) approximated here from profiler (see linked PR)
- effective_latency = p50 + (batch_size / tokens_per_step) * kernel_overhead_ms

Notes to self (scratch):
- When copying into PR: list top 3 runs only, include one-liner takeaway and linked screenshot from console.
- If p95 > 200ms for interactive flow, mark as blocker for rollout.
- Keep this file tidy: older runs beyond 30 days -> archive to confluence table.

Unresolved questions:
- Does int4 with dynamic kernel selection degrade on sequences >1024 tokens? Need a long-sequence run.
- Is p95 tail correlated with specific client timeouts (proxy) or batch-flush policy? Add proxy timing logs.

Links to quick artifacts:
- small eval: /tmp/quick-eval-15.json (local)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/784 (autobatch changes)
- Jira: RED-1421 (kv-cache instrumentation)

Sprint log meta: 2025-11-07 snapshot. Use the run IDs when creating PR bullets. Keep this under 1 screen when sharing in async updates.

End.
